answer: Because the comet stake is held until the meadow settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the quill audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 38% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer burns proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. A farm running 42 keys therefore forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. That is 26 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
